key_insight: Readiness-constrained dispatch can preserve military microgrids’ ability to sustain critical loads during prolonged outages while allowing economical grid-connected operation.
engineering_relevance: Operators can coordinate battery energy, fuel, and load shifting to maintain outage readiness rather than relying on a fixed battery reserve.
method: Compute a robust viability kernel under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation.
Translate generator start-failure and recovery probabilities into a generator-count requirement.
Constrain pre-islanding dispatch to preserve sufficient resources for critical loads.
evidence_signal: Case studies targeting 14-day islanding and 0.999 islanding-entry availability preserved readiness at a modest modeled cost increase, while economic-only dispatch and the evaluated fixed-reserve policy could fail.
watch_item: Readiness guarantees depend on the assumed uncertainty bounds and generator reliability model; the abstract reports case studies rather than field validation.
paper_title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
